content.content: When `deccy new` refuses an unknown `--evaluates` id, the deccy CLI shall name each unknown id in the refusal: every id the invocation gave to `--evaluates` for which the guard finds no node document shall be named, and none of that set left out — not the first unknown id alone, not the last alone, not a sample, not a set cut down by any rule of the naming's own, and not an id passed over because the invocation gave it more than once — and each shall be named by the spelling the invocation gave, so the ids themselves are readable off the refusal rather than a count of them, a set size, the words “an unknown id” said once, a position or an index the caller must resolve elsewhere. The naming shall run over the unknown ones only: no id a node document answers for shall be named in the refusal as unknown, unresolved or missing, and a refusal that quotes the invocation's whole `--evaluates` set while telling apart the ids it answered for from the ids it did not is not naming a resolved id as unknown. The extension of “unknown” shall stay the guard's — the ids no node document answers for, decided by document presence and nothing else — and the naming shall neither widen nor narrow it: no id shall go unnamed because of its kind or content, because it is also given to `--on`, because it appears in some node's `depends_on`, or because it is the root sentinel `zzzzzzzz`, which names no node document and is named with the others whenever the invocation gives it to `--evaluates`. The naming shall be in the refusal itself and not beside it: not on a line following the refusal, not a second message after it, not a hint or usage block offered in its place, not a log line, not an entry under `.deccy/journal/` or in `.deccy/markers.json`, and not a diagnostic the caller runs afterwards. The ids named shall be the `--evaluates` ids and not another flag's: not the ids the invocation gave to `--on`, not the nodes its `depends_on` names, not the summary — and a refusal that names both sets while telling them apart names the `--evaluates` ids. Nothing further shall be read off this requirement: the refusal's message format, the stream it reaches, the order in which the named ids appear, its count wording and its exit status are not fixed here.
content.rationale: Refusing an unknown `--evaluates` id is only repairable if the refusal says which ids failed, so this node fixes the naming and nothing else — the counterpart, for that flag, of nmnlqoyx for `--on`. Its shape follows what the caller would otherwise have to guess: a subset (so the whole unknown set, duplicates included, is named), a count or a pointer (so the spellings are readable off the refusal), a resolved id reported as unknown (so only the unknown ones are named), a place beside the refusal (so the naming is in the refusal itself), and another flag's ids (so the `--evaluates` ids are told apart). When the refusal happens and which ids it covers are mmrklvqs's guard, not this node's; the atomicity that puts the refusal ahead of anything being created is usvvozwn's; the refusal's format, stream and exit status stay with the refusal surface and the invocation-level decisions. The requirement therefore adds one commitment: the set the caller must correct is named in the refusal.
